judgments.reasoning_cat1: One sentence leaving the rate entirely to the commission; 'payable annually or semi-annually' is a closed choice. Nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 12.13's six-percent net-interest ceiling constrains pricing on discounted sales, which this open rate power does not mention; the two are still readable together.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A precise administrative power over place and currency of payment. Nothing indeterminate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 12.6 and 12.11. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Facsimile signature and surviving-signature rules stated with precision. Nothing ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 12.5 and 12.6. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Out of any funds available therefor' is the only soft phrase in an otherwise plain power. Nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 12.18 restricts the use of pledged revenues, which could limit which funds are 'available'; the interaction is implicit but not contradictory.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Requires sale 'on sealed proposals to the highest bidder' yet then permits private sale after rejection of bids, and defines the limit by 'net interest cost' rather than price — the highest-bidder rule and the interest-cost ceiling are two different yardsticks in one provision. That mismatch is arguable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 12.20(b) permits bonds to be delivered to signatory agencies 'notwithstanding any other provision of this compact ... without public offering', expressly displacing this bidding regime. The override is stated, so the tension is managed.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line negotiability rule with a clear exception. Nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 12.5 and 12.6 on registered form. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Declares bonds legal investments for named classes; concrete. Nothing indeterminate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Applies only 'in each of the signatory states', leaving federal fiduciaries unaddressed even though the United States is a signatory party under Section 1.2(h). A small definitional gap.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Conclusive against all persons whomsoever' is sweeping but unmistakable in meaning. Nothing genuinely two-sided.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 15.1(p) gives federal district courts original jurisdiction over compact cases and preserves federal immunity, which qualifies the in rem conclusiveness asserted here. Modest tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Recording, effectiveness and delivery rules stated plainly. Nothing ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 12.6 and 12.18. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A long single sentence in which the exception ('except as and to the extent provided in the indenture with respect to the payment therefrom of expenses for other purposes including ... or other purposes') swallows much of the rule and repeats 'other purposes' twice. The syntax genuinely obscures what may be paid out of the trust fund.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It interacts with Section 12.6's covenant powers and Section 3.7's rate-setting power over the same revenues; those are complementary rather than contradictory.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A structured remedies clause closing with an express non-exclusivity sentence, which forecloses the usual expressio unius argument. Well drafted.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 'Court of competent jurisdiction of any signatory party' is qualified by Section 15.1(p) and New York Section 634, and Section 12.3 bars personal liability; all consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The signatory parties will provide such capital funds ... as may be authorized by their respective statutes' followed by 'nothing in this section shall be deemed to impose any mandatory obligation' is a promise expressly drained of obligation. That self-cancelling structure is a namable defect.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 11.4 requires 'equitable cost sharing and reimbursement formulas' and Section 13.3(c) has the parties 'covenant and agree' to fund the expense budget, so the compact both binds and disclaims funding obligations in different places.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Notwithstanding any other provision of this compact' plus 'subject to and in accordance with the constitutions of the respective signatory parties' is clear in effect. Little ambiguity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It permits guarantees by signatory parties while Section 12.3 says the commission has 'no power to pledge the credit of any signatory party' and Section 12.1 says bonds are payable solely from commission revenues — reconciled only by the notwithstanding clause.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A broad permissive funding provision with plain terms. Nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Duplicates Sections 3.6(g) and 14.13 consistently. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The plan shall include all public and private projects and facilities which are required, in the judgment of the commission' combines a mandatory 'all' with a wholly subjective qualifier, and 'optimum' supplies no measurable standard. Whether a private activity must appear in the plan is genuinely open.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Sections 3.8, 11.1(b) and 11.2(b) make inclusion in the comprehensive plan the gate for undertaking or funding any project, so this provision's breadth determines the reach of the whole regulatory scheme and its fit with Sections 11.1(c) and 11.2(c). It also states the plan duty differently from Section 3.2(a).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The ensuing six years or such other reasonably foreseeable period as the commission may determine' lets the commission displace the stated period at will, which is a namable soft term. Otherwise the duty is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 3.2(b) describes the same program without the six-year benchmark, so the compact states the planning horizon inconsistently in two places. Minor but real.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line content requirement. Nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Mirrors Section 3.2(b). No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'All public and private projects to be anticipated' is loose but purely descriptive of a planning document. Little exposure.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 3.2(b) and 13.1. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short content requirement, plainly stated. Nothing indeterminate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Mirrors Section 3.2(b)'s closing clause. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An annual capital budget requirement with specified contents. Nothing ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 3.2(c) and 12.20(a). No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The apportionment sentence is a long chain ('the amount required to balance ... in addition to the aggregate amount of item (1) above and all other revenues available') that is hard to parse, and 'apportioned equitably' supplies no formula. Both are namable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It requires a 'unanimous vote of the commission' for apportionment while Section 2.5 provides that commission action requires only a majority, so two voting rules govern; and Section 12.20(a) disclaims mandatory funding obligations that this apportionment presupposes.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The parties 'covenant and agree' to include apportioned amounts in their budgets, but 'subject to such review and approval as may be required by their respective budgetary processes' makes the covenant conditional on the promisor's own discretion. That is a genuine self-cancelling promise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 12.20(a) says nothing in that section imposes mandatory obligations on signatory parties, and Section 15.1(e) preserves congressional control over federal appropriations, so the funding covenant is undercut from two directions. The compact's own footnote points to later statutory directives on the same subject.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A permissive stem introducing corporate powers. Nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 2.1's creation of a body corporate. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Contains the obvious typographical error 'enter intro contracts' for 'into contracts'; the slip is visible but does not alter the evident meaning. A mechanical defect of the mildest kind.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 'Sue and be sued in all courts of competent jurisdiction' interacts with Section 15.1(p) and New York Section 634, which define the forum; also with Section 15.1(p)'s preservation of United States immunity. Consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A broad but plainly worded power to receive funds and property. Nothing indeterminate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Duplicates Sections 3.6(g), 12.20(c) and 14.13. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A planning and specification power tied to 'any facility or project', both defined terms. No ambiguity of its own.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its reach follows Sections 1.2(e) and 1.2(g), whose breadth is contested, but this clause adds nothing controversial.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short control power over the commission's own facilities. Nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 3.7 and 14.2(a). No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Long verb and method lists ending with 'or otherwise as it may deem necessary' and 'necessary, useful or convenient' — general catch-alls after specifics, though in a purely enabling clause. Mild list-scope exposure.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 14.14's condemnation power and Section 12.18's restrictions on disposing of pledged facilities both bear on the same subject; they qualify rather than contradict this grant.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'All corporate powers essential to the declared objects and purposes of the commission' is a residual catch-all closing an enumerated list, with 'essential' and 'declared objects' both undefined. That is a namable general-versus-specific problem.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It duplicates Section 3.6(h)'s implied-powers catch-all, and read broadly both would override the specific limits in Sections 3.5, 7.4(b), 8.2(b) and 11. The compact thus contains two open-ended residual grants against several express restrictions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A stem subjecting the commissioners' functions to the compact. Nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 2.2 and 2.5. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Except as otherwise provided by or pursuant to this compact' is a standard qualifier on a governing-body clause. Nothing indeterminate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 2.5 and 14.5(a) on delegation to the executive director. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Subject to any provisions of law specifically applicable to agencies or instrumentalities created by compact' points at an undefined body of law. That reference is vague but consequential only at the margin.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 15.1(m) declares the commission not a federal agency for certain federal statutes, which bears on what law is 'specifically applicable'. Complementary rather than conflicting.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short internal-administration duty. Nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 2.6. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Principal officers' is undefined, leaving unclear which appointments belong to the commissioners. A small namable gap.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 14.5(a) says the executive director appoints 'all other officers and employees' and is himself appointed by the commission, which mostly fills the gap but does not define 'principal officers'. Mild tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A broad personnel power qualified by 'subject to the provisions of this article'. Nothing genuinely two-sided.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 14.5(b)'s merit requirement and Section 15.1(n)'s exclusion of federal employee status both qualify it consistently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line contracting power. Nothing indeterminate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 14.9's bidding requirements and Section 14.8(c)'s voiding of conflicted contracts qualify it expressly. Consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A two-word permissive stem. Nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Introduces (a) and (b); no tension of its own.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Reasonable rules and regulations' and the exclusion for rules dealing 'solely with the internal management of the commission' are both soft boundaries, and the filing requirement's effect on validity is stated in absolute terms. The internal-management carve-out is the namable term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It requires filing under each signatory party's administrative law before a rule is effective, which sits awkwardly with Section 3.7's grant of rate power 'without regulation or control by any department, office or agency of any signatory party' and with Section 14.17's penal sanction for violating any commission rule.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Vesting commission employees with 'the powers of a peace officer of the state' is a striking grant whose content depends entirely on unspecified state law. The scope of those powers is genuinely open.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 14.17 leaves penal sanctions to signatory-state statutes and Section 15.1(m) denies federal agency status, so enforcement authority is distributed across sovereigns without a coordinating rule. That is a structural loose end rather than a flat conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The in-lieu payment formula — payments 'which shall equal the taxes lawfully assessed upon property for the tax year next prior to its acquisition by the commission for a period of ten years' — has a dangling 'for a period of ten years' whose attachment is unclear, and the review standard ('reasonable amount ... hardships incurred and benefits received') is open. Both are namable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 11.3 reserves to the signatory parties the right to levy taxes on withdrawals and Section 12.8 exempts bonds from signatory taxation, so three provisions divide taxing authority without a stated priority; Section 11.4(d)(ii) also addresses payments in lieu of taxes.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'All meetings of the commission shall be open to the public' is absolute and unqualified — no exception for deliberation, personnel or litigation matters. The absence of exceptions is itself a construable feature.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.6 lets the commission adopt its own meeting rules and Section 14.2(a) exempts internal-management rules from hearing requirements, which sit uneasily with an unqualified open-meetings command. The tension is modest.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A detailed notice-and-hearing rule with a closed list plus 'all other cases wherein this compact requires a public hearing'. The catch-all points to identifiable sections rather than being open-ended.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coordinates Sections 4.4, 5.2, 6.2(b), 8.4, 9.4, 10.2, 10.4 and 13.1, all of which require hearings; Section 4.4 additionally requires a hearing on each project. Consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single public-records sentence. Nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 14.4(a). No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'A majority of the full membership' is precise. Nothing genuinely ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.5 requires only 'a majority of the membership' for commission action, so the compact uses two slightly different formulations of the same quorum concept. The difference is unlikely to matter.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Solely on the basis of merit and fitness' and 'found by the commission to be guilty of a violation' are broad, and removal is mandatory with no procedure specified. Namable but conventional.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Sections 14.8(b) and 14.11(d) contain parallel automatic-forfeiture rules with no hearing requirement either, so the compact is at least internally consistent in this respect.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A clear oath requirement with a fixed deadline. Nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Applies to the executive director and his appointees but not to commissioners, an omission Section 14.1(b) does not address. Minor gap.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Each officer shall give such bond ... as the commission may require' leaves everything to the commission but says so plainly. Nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 14.1(b)(5) and 14.5(a). No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A stem introducing three prohibitions. Nothing indeterminate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 14.8(b)-(d). No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Financially interested, either directly or indirectly' is a famously elastic conflict-of-interest formula with no de minimis or attribution rules. 'Indirectly' is the namable term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 14.8(c) voids any contract 'knowingly made in contravention of this section', so the breadth of 'indirectly' has real consequences elsewhere in the article. That amplifies rather than resolves the vagueness.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Money or any other thing of value in addition to the compensation or expenses paid him by the commission' is broad but its meaning is clear. Little to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 15.1(r) permits the federal member and advisor to be compensated by the United States, which is 'in addition to' commission compensation — an apparent overlap with this prohibition, though 15.1(r) is expressly a notwithstanding provision.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A narrow bribery prohibition, plainly worded. Nothing indeterminate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 14.8(b) and 14.8(d). No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Automatic forfeiture on wilful violation; 'willfully' is a familiar standard and 'shall forfeit' is self-executing with no process specified. Mild openness.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Paragraph (a) covers 'no commissioner, officer or employee' but this forfeiture sentence reaches only 'any officer or employee', omitting commissioners — a genuine gap between adjacent paragraphs of the same section.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Knowingly made in contravention of this section is void' — clear rule, though 'knowingly' by whom is unstated. Modest ambiguity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It voids contracts that Sections 14.1(b)(6) and 14.9 authorise the commission to let, with no protection for innocent counterparties; the sections do not address each other.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A savings clause layering federal and state sanctions on top of this section. Nothing genuinely ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 15.1(n) says commission employees are not federal officers or employees, which complicates the reference to sanctions 'imposed by federal law' for misconduct in office. That is a real if narrow mismatch.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Long procurement provision whose obligations are stated in fixed dollar thresholds and whose exceptions are enumerated; 'lowest responsible bidder' and 'in a manner reasonably likely to attract prospective bidders' are the soft terms. Generally definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 8.4 imposes a stricter, waiver-free sealed-bid regime for concessions and Section 15.1(i)-(j) add federal labour and Walsh-Healey requirements to commission contracts; those overlay rather than contradict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A concrete waiver ground for intergovernmental purchases. Nothing indeterminate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 1.5 and 3.9(b). No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The public exigency requires the immediate delivery' is an open standard applied by the commission to itself. That phrase is namable but conventional in procurement law.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No other provision defines public exigency; Section 10.4's emergency machinery is unrelated. No conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Only one source of supply is available' is a short factual test. Nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the rest of Section 14.9. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Of a technical nature' and 'in the public interest' are elastic, and the waiver depends on the commission's own assessment of necessity. Namable soft terms.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No other provision constrains these waivers; Section 14.11's audit is the only check. No conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Specialized or professional nature' is an undefined and famously elastic exemption category that could swallow much of the bidding requirement. That is a genuine list-scope problem.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits against the mandatory bidding rule in the same section's stem, whose $2,500 services threshold it can override without limit. That internal tension is real but familiar.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Contains 'premiums therefore' for 'therefor' and insures 'against loss of revenue from any cause whatsoever', an unbounded phrase. Both are visible but consequence-light defects.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 'Subject to the requirements of any agreement arising out of the issuance of bonds' expressly subordinates it to Sections 12.6 and 12.18. Consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'As soon as practical after the closing of the fiscal year' sets no deadline, and 'accepted accounting practices' is a loose standard. Both are namable but minor.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Paragraphs (b) and (c) add signatory and GAO audits on top of this independent audit, producing three overlapping audit regimes with no coordination rule. That layering is untidy but not contradictory.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An unqualified inspection right 'at any time' over all commission papers and property; sweeping but unmistakable. Nothing genuinely two-sided.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: New York Section 640 implements this paragraph by naming the state comptroller, and Section 14.11(c) adds a federal audit; all consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Subjects the commission's finances to General Accounting Office audit under commercial-corporate principles; the reference to a specific federal auditor is definite though dated. Little internal ambiguity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 15.1(m) provides that for specified federal statutes 'the commission shall not be considered a Federal agency', and Section 15.1(e) preserves federal budgetary authority, so federal oversight is asserted here and disclaimed there. A genuine cross-provision tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The text reads 'refuse to give all require assistance' — a mechanical error for 'all required assistance' — inside a provision imposing automatic forfeiture of office. The defect is on the face of the sentence and affects the described duty.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It parallels the automatic-forfeiture rules in Sections 14.5(b) and 14.8(b) and applies to officers and employees but not commissioners, consistent with the pattern elsewhere.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An annual reporting duty plus discretionary publications. Nothing indeterminate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 15.1(q) reserves to Congress the right to demand disclosure, a cumulative addition. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A permissive stem for state and local funding. Nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 12.20(c) and 14.1(a)(2). No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Preliminary expenses such as' introduces examples rather than a closed list, leaving the category's edge undefined. A minor list-scope point.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 12.2 and 12.20(c). No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Necessary or convenient' is soft but the provision is purely enabling. Little exposure.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 14.13(b) governs repayment of these loans consistently. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'For benefits received or to be received' is broad but permissive only. Nothing genuinely ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 11.4 and 4.3's benefit-based assessments. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A repayment obligation whose period and terms are left to later agreement, which makes the obligation indefinite as drafted. That indefiniteness is namable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 12.1 says bonds are payable solely out of commission properties and revenues, which is consistent with repayment 'out of other income of the commission'. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Includes but is not limited to the power to condemn ... any property already devoted to a public use, by whomsoever owned or held, other than property of a signatory party and ...' packs a general grant, an express extension and two exclusions into one sentence whose exclusions' reach is unclear. The public-utility proviso adds a further conditional layer.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The carve-out for decree-related diversion property tracks Sections 3.5(a) and 3.5(c), and Section 14.15 handles conveyances by signatory parties whose property cannot be condemned; the pieces fit, if awkwardly.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A clear choice-of-law rule with a stated fallback. Nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 14.14(a) and Section 15.1(p)'s jurisdictional provision. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Allocates condemnation awards entirely to the commission in plain terms. Nothing indeterminate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 12.3 and 15.1(g), which likewise insulate signatory parties from commission obligations. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Necessary or convenient to the effectuation of the authorized purposes of the commission' is elastic, but the clause is permissive and process-bound. Modest exposure.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It complements Section 14.14(a)'s exclusion of signatory property from condemnation by supplying a voluntary route. Consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Notwithstanding any contrary provision of law' combined with conveyance 'upon the commission's request' is sweeping, and it is unclear whether the political subdivision retains discretion. That is a genuine ambiguity about whether the power is optional.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Paragraph (a) makes signatory conveyances discretionary and 'in accordance with the laws of the respective parties', whereas this paragraph overrides contrary law for subdivisions — an asymmetry between adjacent paragraphs. Section 14.14(a) also permits condemnation of subdivision property, which would be unnecessary if conveyance were compulsory.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Shall not in any event exceed the expenditure required to serve the public convenience and necessity' is an unmeasurable cap on relocation cost, and 'deemed necessary by the commission' is self-judging. Both are namable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Cost allocation is otherwise governed by Section 11.4's formulas and Section 1.2(d)'s definition of 'cost', which this proviso does not track. Mild disconnect.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A grant of street and highway rights of way 'subject to such reasonable conditions as the highway department of the signatory party may require'. 'Reasonable conditions' is soft but conventional.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coexists with Section 14.15(c) on relocation of dislocated highways and with Section 2.7's basin limit on commission action. No conflict located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Criminal liability attaches to violating 'any provision of this compact or any rule, regulation or order', with the penalty 'to be fixed by the court which the commission may recover in its own name' — a garbled relative clause, and the section labels a civil penalty a penal sanction. Both the breadth and the syntax are construable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It depends on Section 14.2(a)'s rules, which are ineffective until filed under each party's administrative law, and on the undefined 'court of competent jurisdiction' addressed only in New York Section 634. The compact never states which sovereign's substantive law supplies the offence.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Liability exists 'only to the extent and subject to the procedures prescribed by law generally with respect to officers, agents and employees of the government of the United States' — a borrowed liability regime that the compact never identifies, and 'law generally' is indeterminate. That reference is the namable defect.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 15.1(m) provides that for the Federal Tort Claims Act statutes (28 U.S.C. ch. 171 and 1346(b)) 'the commission shall not be considered a Federal agency', and Section 15.1(n) says its employees are not federal employees, so the very regime this section borrows is disapplied elsewhere. That is a specific and serious cross-provision conflict.
